title: vpn on linux: VPN connects but internal names don't resolve (split DNS)
scenario: On linux, a remote-access/VPN problem: VPN connects but internal names don't resolve (split DNS). Symptom: 'connected but internal hosts unreachable by name'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'vpn_split_dns' for vpn on linux
expected_reasoning: VPN up + IP reachable + names failing = the tunnel didn't install the internal DNS/search domains.
Inspect the effective resolver and routes the VPN pushed; confirm the internal domain is routed to the internal DNS.
Fix the split-DNS config so internal names use internal resolvers.
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The 'VPN connects but internal names don't resolve (split DNS)' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('vpn_split_dns') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.

ground_truth.signal: connected but internal hosts unreachable by name

possible_mistakes: Route ALL DNS to the internal resolver, breaking public resolution.
Add a default route through the VPN when only split routes are wanted.
hints: Per-domain (split) DNS sends only the internal zone to the internal resolver.
Check what the tunnel actually pushed vs what's needed.
reference_solution: Configure split-DNS for the internal domain
alternative_solution: Use the VPN client's own split-tunnel/split-DNS profile rather than editing the OS resolver.
edge_cases: Two active interfaces race on DNS priority; the metric decides who wins.
goal: Accesso remoto/VPN: VPN connects but internal names don't resolve (split DNS). Ripristina la connettivita' senza rompere il resto della rete.
